answer: Tie identity to staked reputation that depreciates on churn. Each agent locks a small bond before it can attest; the bond vests over time, like an orchard that only bears fruit after seasons of care, so a farmer who plants a dune of fresh identities gains nothing - sand yields no harvest. When a sybil cluster is detected, its entire stake is slashed and resold, making mass fake accounts economically sable: costly to breed, worthless to keep. One real, long-lived identity outweighs a hundred disposable ones.
